_tsCurrentComment: KNOWN, DOCUMENTED DIVERGENCE -- read this before 'fixing' either side.
derivedIslandEdges above is the contract-correct output: DOMAIN-KJ-01
(02_Architecture/schemas.md 3.3.1) makes 'causal' the one DIRECTED edge type and forbids
pair normalization for it in aggregation, while allowing it for the undirected types.
normalizeUndirectedIslands() for every type with no causal exemption, so it (a) reverses
the isl-b -> isl-a causal pair to isl-a -> isl-b and (b) keys it identically to the
opposite-direction rows, collapsing all three causal edges into ONE aggregate of 3.
This is a PRE-EXISTING TS bug, not drift introduced by AI-IR-PROJECTION-01; it is filed as
tsCurrentDerivedIslandEdges pins what TS produces TODAY so the divergence is enumerated
rather than merely asserted. When that issue is fixed, DELETE this array and point the TS
test back at derivedIslandEdges -- the two become identical again.
The two arrays MUST stay identical on every non-causal row; the TS test asserts that, so
any divergence beyond causal fails loudly instead of hiding here.
